title: warden.check.v1
description: Machine-readable result of scripts/check.sh --json. One document per run; fix the findings in stage order, then rerun.

ok.description: True only when every stage ran and passed.

fast.description: Present only for scripts/check.sh --fast: what was checked and why. A fast run is the inner loop, not the gate: stages missing from 'stages' did not run.

base.description: The ref the change was measured against, with its merge-base commit (origin/main@abc123).

full.description: True when --fast fell back to the full gate (see 'why'); packages is then empty and every stage ran.

why.description: Why it fell back to the full gate.

packages.description: The packages vet, lint and test ran on.

ignored.description: Changed files outside every Go package (docs, scripts), which no stage covers.

name.description: format, vet, lint, roadmap, build, vulncheck, test, fuzz, benchmark, coverage, integration (and, later, archtest, scenarios, ...).

tool.description: The tool with its version, e.g. golangci-lint@v2.12.2.

ok.description: True when the stage ran and has no error finding.

skipped.description: The stage did not run (an earlier stage failed without --keep-going, or it could not be evaluated). A skipped stage is never ok.

metrics.description: Stage numbers. coverage: total, min (percent) and lowest (the five lowest-covered packages). fuzz: targets, fuzzTimePerTarget and fuzzBudgetSeconds (targets x time: the most the stage adds to a run).

rule.description: Stable id, e.g. staticcheck/SA1019, vet/printf, test/data-race, GO-2026-5030, stage/crashed.

file.description: Repo-relative path, when the finding has a location.

fix.description: What to do about it, not only what failed.

output.description: Short tool-output excerpt, capped at 4 KiB and scrubbed of secrets.
